summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Takeuchi studied at Ryukoku University, where he later served as professor emeritus (attested 1987–1995).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology, Watanabe studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Ernst Leumann, and earned a degree from Toyo University. He held professorships at Taisho and Toyo Universities.

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, Bando studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg (1984–1986). In 1987, he held appointments at the Abhidharma Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Katsura studied at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto under Anthony Kennedy Warder. He was Emeritus Professor of Indian Philosophy at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Director at Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Fukihara studied at Horyuji Kangakuin under Join Saeki and at Otani University under Susumu Yamaguchi. He held posts at Otani University (~1948–1964), Doho University (~1954–1964), and Otani University Junior College (~1964–1973).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Ichishima served as Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2014) at Taisho University, and worked as a visiting lecturer in Tibetan Buddhism at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

Kuwayama is a scholar in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1966), where he served as Assistant Professor (~1978–1989) and Professor Emeritus at the Institute for Research in the Humanities.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, Hayashidera has held posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2011) and Hokkaido University, where he is a professor (attested 2026).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Miyamoto studied at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Oxford. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo, Komazawa University, and Waseda University.
Specializing in history, archaeology, and Sinology, Shih was a professor at National Taiwan University (~1990–2007) and served as director of the National Palace Museum (~2004–2006).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Kumoi studied at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna. He taught at Otani University (1948–1981, later emeritus) and Bukkyo University (1982).
Specializing in philosophy and Indology, Saksena held professorships at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
A scholar in Indology and linguistics, Sharma was the founder of the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.

An Indologist, Bhandarkar served as Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (1884), permanent Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai (~1884–1911), and Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College (~1911–1915).
An Indologist, Pathak held posts as a Shastri at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1921) and as a Sanskrit teacher at Elphinstone College (attested 1927).

Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, Bahulkar studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale. He has served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and held posts at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth and Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

A scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, Mishra studied under Anantalal Thakur. He served at Banaras Hindu University as Lecturer, Reader, and ultimately Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit (attested 2010).

Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Belvalkar studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1914–1937) and served as Secretary (~1918–1943) and General Editor of the Mahabharata (1948–1961) at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

A scholar in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, Goswami studied at Banaras Hindu University, where he also taught. He was a visiting scholar at Harvard University, founded Sri Caitanya Prema Samsthana, and was affiliated with Vrindaban Research Institute.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Chen earned a PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen Christina Lang, and served there as a teaching assistant in 1996.
